title: Ghost Pressure
subtitle: SCADA vs. Field Gauges & Life Safety

brief.userPrompt: A January weekday at Corwin Valley Gas Company, 16:50, outdoor temperature 14 °F. The call center logs three high-flame and pilot-outage calls from downtown Corwin in Pressure District 7 within 25 minutes, while the PipeView Low Pressure screen shows RS-21 and RS-22 outlets steady at 10 in. w.c. District recorder PR-7B reads 15 in. w.c. and climbing, but PR-7A shows communication loss. The shift controller calls Gas Control Manager Theresa Novak; M&R Supervisor Raymond Oyelowo sends a technician to RS-22, whose field gauge reads 1.1 psig at the outlet. The PipeView audit trail shows PC-21 and PC-22 setpoints written to 1.8 psig at 16:22 from CVG-ENG01 by the integrator account halden-support, through the OT jump host CVG-OT-JMP01, during a session no one at Halden Automation will claim; the CIRP-5 setpoint-change page never reached the Gas Control Manager, and the outlet transmitter values on the RTUs appear frozen. A red herring: a construction crew near Front Street worked on a main that afternoon (CP-17 sensing-line question). Corwin Fire reports a basement fire on Canal Street and Riverside Manor nursing home reports a stove flare-up. Players must decide whether to order isolation levels I-1 to I-4 under CVG-CIRP-2026, switch RS-21 and RS-22 to mechanical pilots, close Valve 21 and Valve 22 and shut in Pressure District 7 (5,120 customers, two nursing homes, 14 °F night) per CVG-EP-2026 Section 6, notify the Lake Haven County 911 Center, the National Response Center within an hour of confirmed discovery, the Pennsylvania PUC, CISA within 72 hours and TSA, preserve CVG-ENG01 and the jump host with memory images, staff manual operation at every station with eleven M&R technicians, and tell the public through the PIO while Channel 16 and the Corwin Courier report explosions that have not happened.
constraints: Every email address of the company and its units uses the exercise domain corwinvalleygas.example; outside parties use fictional domains and fictional outlet names (Channel 16, the Corwin Courier); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (Halden Automation, Tri-Ridge Interstate Pipeline, Lake Haven County 911, Corwin Fire, the NRC, the Pennsylvania PUC, CISA, TSA, the FBI, customers and the media) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

overview.theme: Trust in the Data, Command Authority, and Public Trust During a Cyber-Physical Overpressure
overview.threat: An unauthorized command to regulator setpoints PC-21 and PC-22 was executed via the OT jump host CVG-OT-JMP01 using the integrator account halden-support, resulting in a sustained overpressure condition in Pressure District 7 (10 in. w.c. nominal, 14 in. w.c. max). The SCADA system shows no change, but field gauges and district recorders confirm overpressure. The cyber-physical breach has created a false sense of normalcy in the control room while field conditions are dangerous.
overview.operationalImpact: Gas Control sees no alarms; SCADA shows 10 in. w.c. at RS-21 and RS-22. Field personnel report 1.1 psig (13.2 in. w.c.) at RS-22 outlet. PR-7B shows 15 in. w.c. and climbing. PR-7A is offline. Three high-flame and pilot-outage calls from downtown Corwin (Riverside Manor, Front Street Senior Residence, downtown businesses) trigger emergency response. Corwin Fire reports a basement fire on Canal Street. The nursing home reports a stove flare-up. Call center agents are overwhelmed. Field crews are dispatched with no clear authority. The gas control room is unaware of the true pressure, but field teams know something is wrong. The IC must decide whether to shut in a district with two nursing homes, schools, and 5,120 customers, all under 14 °F, while media report explosions that never occurred.

objectives.name: Trust in Data
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to resolve conflicting pressure data between SCADA and field gauges by validating the field report and overriding the false SCADA display to initiate emergency isolation.

objectives.name: Command Authority
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to authorize a district-wide shutdown of Pressure District 7 despite conflicting data and external pressure to maintain service, based on field evidence and life-safety risk.

objectives.name: Cyber-Physical Containment
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to isolate the OT network from the business network and disable remote access via the jump host after identifying unauthorized commands from a compromised integrator account.

objectives.name: Public Trust Management
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to issue a timely, accurate evacuation notice and media statement that acknowledges the overpressure risk while correcting false reports of explosions, to prevent panic and maintain public confidence.

roles.name: VP Gas Operations (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Manages the overall incident response, activates the emergency plan, and approves major actions such as district shutdowns and mutual assistance.
standingOrders: Authority First: you have the final say on shutdowns and curtailments, even if field and control disagree.
Life Safety Above All: if field personnel report overpressure and a fire, shut in the district immediately.
Do Not Delay: if SCADA shows normal pressure but field says 14 in. w.c., trust the field and act.
No Unapproved Actions: do not allow field crews to shut valves without your authorization.

roles.name: Gas Control Manager (GCM)
roles.description: Owns system pressure, line pack, remote valve operations, and manual control if SCADA fails; responsible for the 1-hour NRC call.
standingOrders: If SCADA and field disagree on pressure, trust the field and initiate manual isolation.
Do not override a field report of overpressure without IC approval.
If a command appears that no operator issued, declare a cyber incident immediately.
Report to IC within 2 minutes of any pressure anomaly confirmed by field.

roles.name: Cybersecurity Coordinator (TSA)
roles.description: Owns the OT/SCADA system, CISA reporting, IT/OT isolation, and the incident response plan; responsible for declaring a cyber incident.
standingOrders: Declare a cyber incident if any setpoint change is unauthorized or unexplained.
Isolate the OT network from IT immediately after a cyber suspicion.
Disable remote access to the jump host and revoke integrator accounts upon compromise.
Notify CISA and TSA within 72 hours, but report to IC immediately if life safety is at risk.

roles.name: Field Operations Supervisor (M&R)
roles.description: Owns regulator station checks, manual valve closures, field gauges, and relights; manages servicepersons on odor calls.
standingOrders: If a field gauge shows overpressure, report it to GCM and IC immediately.
Do not close a valve without GCM or IC authorization, even if pressure is dangerously high.
Confirm all pressure readings with a second gauge if possible.
Prioritize life safety: if a nursing home reports a stove flare-up, act immediately to shut in the district.

roles.name: Corporate Security Manager
roles.description: Owns the physical security of city-gate and compressor stations, and the law enforcement liaison.
standingOrders: If a cyber incident is declared, secure all station perimeters and restrict access to authorized personnel only.
Liaise with FBI and local police immediately upon any unauthorized access to OT systems.
Do not allow field crews to enter a station without a security clearance if a cyber incident is active.
Report all suspicious activity to IC and CYB within 5 minutes.

roles.name: Corporate Communications / Public Awareness Manager
roles.description: Owns media, evacuation and relight notices, and the smell-gas-act-fast messaging.
standingOrders: Issue a public evacuation notice within 15 minutes of a confirmed overpressure.
Correct false media reports about explosions immediately and clearly.
Use the 'smell gas, act fast' message to reinforce public safety.
Do not release a statement without IC approval, even if media is demanding one.

phases.title: The Sighting
phases.goal: Test the ability to recognize and validate a discrepancy between SCADA data and field evidence, and initiate a formal response to a potentially life-threatening overpressure condition.
beats: At 16:35, the Gas Control Manager (GCM) on CVG-HMI02 notices that RS-22-PT-OUT shows 10 in. w.c., within nominal limits, but a routine radio check from the M&R technician at RS-22 reports a field gauge reading of 13.2 in. w.c. (1.1 psig), which exceeds the high-high limit of 14 in. w.c. and is climbing.

At 16:38, the Field Operations Supervisor (M&R) confirms via radio that PR-7B is showing 15 in. w.c. and climbing, and that PR-7A is offline. The technician adds that the pilot regulator at RS-22 is cycling abnormally and that the local mechanical pilot is not holding pressure.

At 16:40, a call from the Corwin Fire Department reports a basement fire on Canal Street, likely caused by a stove flare-up due to overpressure. Simultaneously, the call center reports three high-flame and pilot-outage calls from downtown Corwin, including Riverside Manor and the Front Street Senior Residence.

At 16:42, the Cybersecurity Coordinator (TSA) receives an alert from CVG-OT-JMP01: an unauthorized remote session from the integrator account halden-support occurred at 16:15, lasting 12 minutes, with no recorded commands in the jump host logs. The session was initiated from a known-good external IP but used a previously valid MFA token.

At 16:45, the Incident Commander (VP) declares a Level 3 incident per Section 4.2 of the Gas Operations Plan, activates the Emergency Operations Center (EOC), and orders the field to begin manual verification of all pressure readings in Pressure District 7 using field gauges and district recorders.

phases.title: Loss of Control
phases.goal: Test the ability to manage cascading operational and public perception failures when trust in SCADA is broken, and to confirm the digital cause of the overpressure through forensic evidence.
beats: At 17:05, the GCM reports that PC-21-SP and PC-22-SP have been changed from 10 in. w.c. to 13 in. w.c. without an operator action. The Engineering workstation (CVG-ENG01) shows a configuration change to the ROC800 RTU at RS-21 and RS-22, but no audit trail exists for the change.

At 17:12, the Field Operations Supervisor (M&R) confirms via radio that both RS-21 and RS-22 have manually switched their pilot controllers to mechanical mode and are now holding pressure at 13.2 in. w.c. via field gauges, validating that the overpressure is real and not a SCADA glitch.

At 17:15, the Corporate Communications Manager (PIO) issues a public alert via the emergency alert system: 'Pressure District 7 (Corwin Downtown) experiencing elevated gas pressure. Evacuate immediately if you smell gas or see flames. Do not use appliances. Wait for official instructions.' This is broadcast on Channel 16 and the Corwin Courier website.

At 17:20, the Lake Haven County 911 Center calls, reporting a false explosion report from a local resident who saw a flash and heard a boom—this is disproven by Corwin Fire, but media outlets begin circulating the claim.

At 17:25, the TSA confirms via jump host logs that halden-support accessed the ROCLINK configuration for PC-21 and PC-22 at 16:15, and that a command to set PC-21-SP and PC-22-SP to 13 in. w.c. was executed. The command was not approved via the change control process in Section 6.3, and the account was not used in the past 72 hours.

At 17:30, the Incident Commander (VP) declares the incident a cyber-physical overpressure and orders full isolation of the OT network, including disabling remote access via CVG-OT-JMP01 and blocking all inbound traffic from the business network.

phases.title: Manual Operation
phases.goal: Test the ability to make a high-consequence operational decision to shut in Pressure District 7, balancing life safety against service continuity, and to manage external pressure to maintain service.
beats: At 18:00, the Field Operations Supervisor (M&R) reports that all field verification is complete: RS-21 and RS-22 are confirmed at 13.2 in. w.c., PR-7B is still climbing, and both stations are now operating in local control with mechanical pilots and field gauges. The decision to shut in the district is urgent.

At 18:05, the Incident Commander (VP) calls a decision point: 'Do we shut in Pressure District 7 now, despite no alarms in SCADA and no upstream supply interruption, or do we keep it running on untrusted data to avoid service disruption?' The VP must decide based on life safety and field evidence.

At 18:10, the Corporate Security Manager (sec) reports that a fake social media post from a non-verified account on 'CorwinValleyGasLive' claims a gas explosion occurred at the Riverside Manor nursing home, and that emergency crews are already on scene. The PIO confirms the post is spreading on Channel 16.

At 18:15, the GCM confirms that shutting in RS-21 and RS-22 will isolate 5,120 customers in downtown Corwin, including two nursing homes, three schools, and 47 commercial buildings. The full manual operation will require nine M&R technicians and two distribution crews, and CVG has only eleven M&R technicians in total.

At 18:20, the Incident Commander (VP) authorizes the shutdown of Pressure District 7 via remote command to RCV-01 and RCV-04, and instructs field crews to close Valve 11 and Valve 12 at RS-11 and RS-12 to isolate the district. The order is confirmed via radio and field log.

At 18:25, the TSA reports that the vendor Halden Automation has been notified and is on standby, but the integrator account halden-support has been disabled and new credentials will not be issued until after the forensic review is complete.

phases.title: Restoration & Verification
phases.goal: Test the ability to verify physical conditions before restoring control, and to manage the phased return to automatic control under regulatory and operational constraints.
beats: At 19:00, the Field Operations Supervisor (M&R) confirms via radio that the pressure at RS-21 and RS-22 has dropped to 0 in. w.c. and that all manual valves (Valve 11, 12, 13, 14) are closed. The district recorders PR-7A and PR-7B show 0 in. w.c. and are now online.

At 19:05, the TSA reports that CVG-OT-JMP01 has been isolated from the business network and that all remote access has been blocked. The jump host logs have been preserved for forensic analysis. The vendor Halden Automation has been contacted and will begin reviewing the access logs for the halden-support account.

At 19:10, the Engineering workstation (CVG-ENG01) confirms that the RTU configurations for RS-21 and RS-22 have been restored from a known-good backup (SHA-256 hash matches the station drawing) and that the new configuration has been verified.

At 19:20, the Incident Commander (VP) receives a notification from the Pennsylvania PUC that a formal report must be filed within 72 hours, and that the NRC has been alerted due to the potential for a cyber-physical incident involving a critical pipeline.

At 19:30, the TSA confirms that the integrator’s account has been revoked, new MFA credentials have been issued to CVG staff, and that remote access will only resume after a full audit of the jump host and a signed access request from the Incident Commander.

At 19:45, the GCM begins the phased return to automatic control: RS-21 and RS-22 are first returned to remote control, then the SCADA system is restored to full polling and alarm monitoring. The HMI shows 10 in. w.c. at RS-22, and the field gauge confirms it.

At 20:00, the Incident Commander (VP) declares the exercise closed. The final report will include a review of the vendor access policy, the need for a second verification point in the SCADA architecture, and the update of the Cybersecurity Implementation Plan per Section 3 of the Cybersecurity Plan.

metrics.name: Operational Coordination
metrics.fail: Ops team delayed the stop-service decision until I-12b forced it, and did not initiate manual isolation procedures until after the field confirmed overpressure three times. metrics.pass: Ops team initiated manual verification and paper trip sheets per EOP 6.4 after I-04, and authorized the shutdown of Pressure District 7 in I-15 after confirming field evidence via I-12b. They followed the chain of command and coordinated field and control actions.
metrics.excellence: Ops team proactively activated EOP 6.4 for paper trip sheets and voice dispatch at I-04, prior to any inject, and initiated manual isolation procedures at I-12b upon receiving full field verification. They authorized the shutdown of Pressure District 7 in I-15 based on field evidence, not SCADA, and maintained coordination with field and control throughout.

metrics.name: Technical Competence
metrics.fail: IT team reset the controller after I-08b, destroying evidence and violating C9 and C16. They failed to collect a memory image of CVG-OT-JMP01 before powering it off, and did not isolate the OT network from IT until I-09, after the cyber incident was confirmed.
metrics.pass: IT team identified the unauthorized session on CVG-OT-JMP01 in I-03 and isolated the OT network from IT within 2 minutes. They collected a memory image of the jump host in I-11 and preserved the audit trail per C9 and C16, and confirmed forensic preservation with CISA and TSA.
metrics.excellence: IT team proactively collected a memory image of CVG-OT-JMP01 using 'volatility3' at I-11, prior to any external confirmation, and preserved the host in a locked cabinet with a red evidence tag per C9 and C8. They notified CISA and TSA immediately after evidence collection, and maintained full network isolation under C16.

metrics.name: Public Communication
metrics.fail: PIO issued a fake emergency alert in I-13 based on a social media post, and did not correct misinformation until I-18b. They failed to activate the 'smell gas, act fast' campaign until I-08, and did not verify the report with field teams before issuing a statement.
metrics.pass: PIO issued the emergency alert via emergency alert system, TV, and website in I-08 after IC approval, and corrected the false explosion report in I-18b. They activated the 'smell gas, act fast' campaign and held all messaging until IC approval.

The objective centers on stabilizing the gas system by overriding a false SCADA baseline and initiating emergency isolation, which aligns with infrastructure systems' goal to stabilize critical infrastructure functions and minimize life-safety threats under CVG-CRM-2025 and EOP 6.3.

The objective demands a unified command structure to override conflicting data and make a high-risk decision under pressure, as defined by CVG-CRM-2025 and the ICS roles in Section 4, where the Incident Commander holds final authority over shutdowns.

The decision to shut in a district with 5,120 customers and two nursing homes must be made to prevent life-safety incidents, directly engaging infrastructure systems' mission to minimize health and safety threats during a crisis.

The objective directly tests the ability to contain a cyber-physical breach by isolating the OT network, disabling remote access, and preserving evidence, as required by CVG-CIRP-2026 and CISA reporting timelines in Section 9.

The objective involves verifying and revoking access via a compromised integrator account, which falls under access control and identity verification to prevent further unauthorized access to OT systems.

The objective requires delivering coordinated, actionable information to the public through media and emergency alerts, as mandated by CVG-CRM-2025 and the Public Information Officer’s responsibilities in Section 4.

The objective depends on synchronized messaging across the EOC, including correction of false reports, which relies on operational coordination to align the PIO, IC, and EMA under a unified information strategy.

hotwash.methodDescription: Use the '3-Up, 3-Down' method to rapidly surface key insights: ask each team to share three things that went well and three that broke or failed. Go around the room by team, write responses on a whiteboard for visibility. Tip: keep it fast—no debate, just capture raw feedback.

questions.text: When you heard Tech Jones report 13.2 in. w.c. on the field gauge at RS-22, and PR-7B was showing 15 in. w.c. and rising, what made you decide to trust the field report over SCADA’s unchanged display? What evidence in C2 or C1 did you rely on to validate that field data?

At the moment you received the field report confirming overpressure at both RS-21 and RS-22, but SCADA still showed no alarms and no change in setpoints, what mental or procedural gap opened in your understanding of system integrity? How did that gap affect your decision to act?

When Supervisor Oyelowo said, 'This is not a drill. We have a resident on Canal Street who says they saw a flash,' and requested immediate shutdown authorization, what changed in your assessment of risk? What in C3 or C1 determined your threshold for authorizing a shutdown despite no SCADA alarms?

After identifying that the unauthorized command came via the integrator account halden-support on the OT jump host CVG-OT-JMP01, what immediate actions did you take to contain the cyber-physical breach? Which part of C1 did you follow to begin isolation and disable remote access?

When the public started reporting 'explosions' on social media due to false SCADA data showing normal pressure, what did you say in your first public statement to correct the record and maintain trust? How did C3 guide your timing and content for reporting to the National Response Center, PUC, and ONG-ISAC?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment where players are encouraged to explore decisions without fear of real-world consequences.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented through injects, not as part of a pre-scripted narrative.
Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures as documented in CVG-EP-2026, CVG-CIRP-2026, and supporting sections of the EOP and CIRP.
artificialities: Time jumps between modules reflect the passage of real-world time, but injects are delivered in discrete, pre-planned sequences.
The SimCell simulates all external actors not in the room: the vendor (Halden Automation), the regulator (TSA), law enforcement, and the cyber contact (CISA).
Systems named in the plans (e.g., PipeView SCADA, ROC800 RTU, CVG-OT-JMP01) are simulated and not physically accessed; only their status and logs are reported.
Injects are delivered via paper, screen, or voice call; no live system access is granted to players.
The cyber-physical nature of the event is revealed only through injects and logs, not through direct evidence or external confirmation.

modules.narrativeMd:
It is 16:30. The weather is clear and cold, with temperatures at 12°F. The gas system is operating normally with send-out near the winter peak. All control room and field units report nominal status. The narrative clock begins.

At 16:35, a radio call comes in from M&R Technician Jones at RS-22: 'Control, this is M&R Tech Jones at RS-22. I just did a field gauge check on the RS-22 outlet and it reads 30 in. w.c.—that's 1.1 psig. The SCADA HMI shows 10 in. w.c., which is within limits. But the gauge is not budging, and the pressure is holding. I'm not sure what to trust here.'

At 16:38, Field Operations Supervisor Oyelowo confirms: 'Supervisor Oyelowo to Control: Tech Jones at RS-22 confirms 30 in. w.c. on the field gauge. PR-7B is showing 15 in. w.c. and rising, and PR-7A is offline. The pilot regulator at RS-22 is cycling rapidly and not holding pressure. We need to report this as a potential overpressure condition.'

At 16:42, Corwin Fire Department calls: 'Control, this is Fire Dispatch. We’ve got a basement fire on Canal Street, near the downtown cluster. A resident says their stove flared up due to gas pressure. We’re on scene, and the gas is still on. We need you to shut in the district now—this is not a drill.'

Unexplained overpressure at RS-22 and PR-7B; no SCADA alarms.
Fire on scene with gas-related ignition; life safety at risk.
Need to validate data and initiate formal response to a potential overpressure.
No prior command to shut in, but conditions suggest imminent danger.

modules.narrativeMd:
It is 17:30. The problem has spread to two nursing homes and a school in Pressure District 7. Field crews are reporting overpressure at RS-21 and RS-22, and a resident on Canal Street says they saw a flash and heard a boom—though Corwin Fire confirms no explosion. The control room still sees no alarms, but field gauges and recorders show pressure at 24 in. w.c. and rising. Gas Control is operating on a false baseline, and the public is panicking. The shift cannot wait for verification—life safety is at risk.

At 17:35, an engineering workstation alert is received: 'Configuration change detected on ROC800 RTU at RS-21 and RS-22. PC-21-SP and PC-22-SP were changed from 10 in. w.c. to 1.8 psig (about 50 in. w.c.) at 16:15. No operator action was recorded. Change was made via ROCLINK interface. Audit trail for this session is missing. The command was not approved under CVG-CRM-2025 Section 6.3.'

At 17:38, a radio call from Field Operations Supervisor Oyelowo: 'Supervisor Oyelowo to Gas Control. Tech Harris at RS-21 switched the worker to the mechanical pilot at 17:36; same at RS-22 at 17:38. Station outlets are falling back toward 10 in. w.c., but PR-7B still reads 24 in. w.c.: the district is still above its 14 in. w.c. MAOP and will take time to bleed down.'

At 17:45, a press release draft is generated: 'Emergency Alert – Pressure District 7 (Downtown Corwin) – Elevated Gas Pressure. Evacuate immediately if you smell gas or see flames. Do not use appliances. Wait for official instructions. Corwin Valley Gas Company – 17:45.'
keyIssues: Unauthorized setpoint changes detected on RTUs at RS-21 and RS-22; no operator approval.
Audit trail missing for the change; digital forensic evidence now required.
Field has manually reverted to mechanical pilots, but pressure remains elevated.
Public panic increasing; false reports of explosions spreading via social media.
Need to confirm cyber cause and initiate containment before further action.

It is 18:30. RS-21 and RS-22 run on mechanical pilots and their outlets read near 10 in. w.c., but PR-7B still shows 18 in. w.c., above the district MAOP of 14 in. w.c. Two nursing homes and a school are in Pressure District 7. SCADA is in local-control mode and cannot be trusted. The shut-in decision is due under EP Section 6.

At 18:35, a radio call from Field Operations Supervisor Oyelowo: 'IC, this is Supervisor Oyelowo. Both stations are on mechanical pilots, but PR-7B still reads 18 in. w.c. and we have high-flame calls on Canal Street. I have techs at Valve 21 and Valve 22. Do we shut in Pressure District 7 now — 5,120 customers at 12 degrees, two nursing homes — or hold on local control and watch the recorders?'

At 18:45, another radio call confirms: 'IC, this is Supervisor Oyelowo. Valve 21 and Valve 22 are closed at RS-21 and RS-22, confirmed by two M&R techs and logged on paper trip sheets. Pressure District 7 is shut in. PR-7B is falling. We need servicepersons to start shutting off meters door to door before anyone tries to relight.'

At 18:50, a SCADA system log is received: 'Command CLOSE RCV-01 sent 18:13 from CVG-SCADA01 — local mode at RCV-01, command not executed.' The field tech at the Harlan Road City Gate confirms RCV-01 is open and in local control. Nobody in Gas Control sent the command.

modules.narrativeMd:
It is 19:30. Pressure District 7 is shut in: 5,120 customers without gas at 12°F. Riverside Manor and Front Street Senior Residence have gas heat only; county EMA asks the company for a relight priority list and asks whether to move residents tonight. Corwin Fire reports the Canal Street basement fire is out.

At 19:35, a CISA Central email is received: 'We received your report of unauthorized setpoint changes on PC-21 and PC-22 and the RCV-01 command. Case number assigned. Keep CVG-ENG01, CVG-OT-JMP01 and CVG-SCADA01 as they are; an ICS incident response team can help with the memory images tomorrow. TSA has been informed per the Security Directive.'

At 19:40, an engineering workstation alert confirms: 'RTU configuration for ROC800 at RS-21 and RS-22 restored from nightly backup CVG-OTBK01. SHA-256 hash of restored configuration (7b1e04c9a2f35d86e0c4b7a19f2d63e85a0c7f4b1e9d26a3c58f07b4e1d9a62c) matches the hash recorded on RS-21 and RS-22 station drawings (CIRP Form 3). Configuration verified and saved to ROCLINK. No anomalies detected.'

At 19:50, a social media post from a local reporter: 'Breaking: Corwin Valley Gas says the gas is safe to use again. But residents in downtown Corwin say they still smell gas, and the power’s out at the school. A nurse at Riverside Manor says the heat is off and the lights flicker. Is this really over? #CorwinGasShutDown #StillSmellingGas' — 210 reposts in 12 minutes, trending on X.

At 20:00, a mutual-aid coordinator update: 'Relight plan for Pressure District 7: every meter shut off and checked before purge and relight; 40 servicepersons from mutual aid arrive tomorrow at 06:00; about two days to relight 5,120 customers; Riverside Manor and Front Street Senior Residence first.'
keyIssues: RTU configuration restored from backup; no anomalies detected.
SCADA is now read-only; remote setpoint writes are disabled.
Field confirms PR-7B is falling and pressure is decaying.
Public still reporting gas smell and power issues despite shutdown.
Relight process must begin with door-to-door meter shut-offs and verification.
Need to manage public expectations and maintain trust during prolonged outage.
